hints: Focus on which functional groups actually react with sodium to release hydrogen gas.
Remember that one $\text{-OH}$ group or one $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ group gives only 0.5 mol of $\text{H}_2$ from 1 mol of compound.
Count the reactive $\text{-OH}$ plus $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ groups in each option and look for the one that totals two reactive hydrogens.
walkthrough:
**Recall how sodium makes hydrogen**

Sodium reacts with any acidic hydrogen in alcohols and carboxylic acids. Each reactive $\text{-OH}$ or $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ provides one H atom.

Reaction rule:
$$2\text{R-OH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{R-ONa} + \text{H}_2$$

**Work out the mole ratio**

From the equation, 2 mol of $\text{-OH}$ groups make 1 mol of $\text{H}_2$. So 1 mol of $\text{-OH}$ makes 0.5 mol of $\text{H}_2$.

Key rule:
$$1 \text{ mol reactive H} \rightarrow 0.5 \text{ mol } \text{H}_2$$

**Apply to the question**

We need 1 mol of $\text{H}_2$ from 1 mol of Y. That needs twice as much hydrogen:
$$1 \text{ mol } \text{H}_2 \text{ needs } 2 \text{ mol reactive H per mol of Y}$$

**Count reactive groups and decide**

Options A, B and C each have only one reactive group, so give only 0.5 mol $\text{H}_2$. Only $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$ has both an alcohol $\text{-OH}$ and a carboxylic acid $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$, giving two reactive H atoms and a full 1 mol of $\text{H}_2$.

options.A: Butan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, has only one alcohol $\text{-OH}$ group. 1 mol gives only 0.5 mol $\text{H}_2$, not 1 mol.
options.B: 2-methylpropan-2-ol, $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_3\text{COH}$, also has only one alcohol $\text{-OH}$ group. Tertiary structure does not change the mole ratio, so it still gives only 0.5 mol $\text{H}_2$.
options.C: Butanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, has only one carboxylic acid $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ group. Although it is more acidic, it still provides only one reactive H, so gives only 0.5 mol $\text{H}_2$.
options.D: Lactic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$, has two reactive groups: one alcohol $\text{-OH}$ and one carboxylic acid $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$. Both react with Na, giving 2 reactive H atoms per molecule, so 1 mol of Y produces 1 mol of $\text{H}_2$.
